title: Commodity hedging
subtitle: Weekly note for corporate hedging conversations: energy, metals, grains
headline: Week of 04 November 2026. Backwardation in Brent Crude, WTI Crude, Aluminium; contango in Natural Gas, Copper, Gold, Silver, Wheat, Corn. Realized vol is high against five years in Brent Crude, WTI Crude, Gold, Silver and low in Natural Gas, Wheat, Soybeans: that is where option hedges are dear and cheap.

sections.title: Energy: what a hedge locks in, and what optionality costs
paragraphs: Brent Crude: backwardation, BZZ27 16.0% below BZF27. A producer selling 11 months forward locks in 16.0% less than the front; a consumer buying forward pays 16.0% less.
WTI Crude: backwardation, CLZ27 15.0% below CLZ26. A producer selling 12 months forward locks in 15.0% less than the front; a consumer buying forward pays 15.0% less.
Natural Gas: contango, NGZ27 32.2% above NGZ26. A consumer buying 12 months forward pays 32.2% more than the front; a producer selling forward locks in 32.2% more.

Brent Crude: realized vol 61%, 92nd percentile of five years. Options-based hedges (puts, collars) are expensive against history; forwards and swaps carry no vol premium. Implied vol is estimated at about 66%: on Bloomberg history since 2015, implied has run 1.08 times realized, with a typical error of 5 points. WTI Crude: realized vol 57%, 88th percentile of five years. Options-based hedges (puts, collars) are expensive against history; forwards and swaps carry no vol premium. Implied vol, which is what an option actually costs, is 59%: close to what has been realized (+1.9 points). Natural Gas: realized vol 50%, 18th percentile of five years. Optionality is cheap against history: the moment to price puts, collars or participating forwards.

sections.title: Metals: what a hedge locks in, and what optionality costs
paragraphs: Copper: contango, HGZ27 5.8% above HGZ26. A consumer buying 12 months forward pays 5.8% more than the front; a producer selling forward locks in 5.8% more.

Aluminium: backwardation, ALIM27 2.8% below ALIZ26. A producer selling 6 months (the furthest contract on the free feed) forward locks in 2.8% less than the front; a consumer buying forward pays 2.8% less.
Gold: contango, GCZ27 4.2% above GCZ26. A consumer buying 12 months forward pays 4.2% more than the front; a producer selling forward locks in 4.2% more.
Silver: contango, SIZ27 4.2% above SIZ26. A consumer buying 12 months forward pays 4.2% more than the front; a producer selling forward locks in 4.2% more.

Copper: realized vol 21%, 37th percentile of five years, in line with history. Aluminium: realized vol 22%, 48th percentile of five years, in line with history. Gold: realized vol 27%, 89th percentile of five years. Options-based hedges (puts, collars) are expensive against history; forwards and swaps carry no vol premium. Implied vol, which is what an option actually costs, is 24%: close to what has been realized (-2.4 points). Silver: realized vol 49%, 88th percentile of five years. Options-based hedges (puts, collars) are expensive against history; forwards and swaps carry no vol premium.

sections.title: Agriculture: what a hedge locks in, and what optionality costs
paragraphs: Wheat: contango, ZWZ27 8.1% above ZWZ26. A consumer buying 12 months forward pays 8.1% more than the front; a producer selling forward locks in 8.1% more.
Corn: contango, ZCZ27 9.1% above ZCZ26. A consumer buying 12 months forward pays 9.1% more than the front; a producer selling forward locks in 9.1% more.
Soybeans: flat curve, ZSX27 within 1.4% of ZSF27: forward hedges lock in roughly today's price.

Wheat: realized vol 16%, 2nd percentile of five years. Optionality is cheap against history: the moment to price puts, collars or participating forwards. Corn: realized vol 17%, 24th percentile of five years, in line with history. Soybeans: realized vol 8%, 0th percentile of five years. Optionality is cheap against history: the moment to price puts, collars or participating forwards.

paragraphs: Contracts closest to 6 and 12 months after the front; gas and grains compare the same season. Where the free feed stops before 12 months, the shape is read on the furthest contract.

paragraphs: Realized vol of the front-month series over 21 sessions, with its percentile over one and five years. Implied only where CBOE publishes it.

sections.title: How the free contracts track the European benchmarks
paragraphs: Measured once on Bloomberg history, weekly returns since November 2021. A ratio above 1 means the free contract is more volatile than the benchmark a European client hedges.

method: Talking points rank markets by how far their 12-month curve or their realized-vol percentile sits from normal. Context for client conversations, not a recommendation.
caveats: Free data: Yahoo Finance closes of NYMEX, COMEX and CBOT futures. Copper and aluminium are COMEX contracts, not LME; Brent is the NYMEX last-day financial contract. No TTF, power, coal, softs or pulp on the free feed.

Implied vol history exists only for WTI (OVX) and gold (GVZ). Brent's implied vol is estimated from realized with a ratio calibrated on Bloomberg history (typical error about 5 points, much more in stress); elsewhere the realized-vol percentile stands in for what options cost, which holds only if implied tracks realized.
The free contracts are US benchmarks: Henry Hub barely tracks European gas (TTF), and COMEX copper and CBOT wheat are more volatile than their LME and Euronext counterparts (see the table above).
The front-month series rolls from contract to contract, so weekly and monthly moves include roll gaps.

Curves come from listed contracts only (12 to 13 months out, fewer for grains and aluminium), not from swap curves. Deferred metal contracts trade thinly, so intermediate points can be noisy; the 12-month comparison uses the same delivery month a year later, usually the most liquid.

calculator.note: Black-76 on the future, one flat vol for every strike and tenor, option expiry approximated to the 20th of the month before delivery (Brent: two months before). A desk prices off the smile: puts would come out dearer and the free cap of a collar lower. Indicative, not a quote.
